entry.title: On Giving Up
entry.summary:
Today in the drum class, I gave up playing the song I was practicing. I had already spent three days learning it, and still couldn’t play it properly. In particular, I couldn’t keep the right tempo. I realized that I shouldn’t try anymore, and decided to give up on it.
Work Hard, Dream Big, Never Give Up1
I am largely an autodidact in many interests of my life. I taught myself programming, reading music, running etc by reading books, watching videos, listening to people. A big part of learning by oneself is knowing when to give up. There are many things in my life that I’ve walked way from. Let me list a few2: Playing video games
As I child I loved playing video games, but upon growing up I decided to stop. I realized that they were too addictive for me, and for the kind of person I am…

entry.title: tugz: a new deflate library with three applications
entry.summary:
I spent a week creating a new deflate implementation from scratch in C named tugz to provide an Info-ZIP-compatible zip program for w64devkit 2.10.1 (released today). I also replaced busybox-w32’s deflate-based unzip, gzip, gunzip, and zcat apps as well. My new deflate performs much better than zlib and on par with libdeflate. In general the new programs are substantially faster and produce slightly smaller outputs than the BusyBox equivalents, which is optimized for size than speed after all, but also compared to the original gzip and Info-ZIP you get in a typical Linux distribution. The tugz programs are CRT-free (inspect them with peports!) with first-class Windows support and better Unicode handling.
Besides the cute logo, tugz is public domain and written entirely in my personal styl…

entry.summary: My blog began as a blosxom (Perl) site running on a VPS. In 2011 I moved to the new GitHub Pages, with the site generated statically by Jekyll (Ruby) on a GitHub server. It was a no-brainer: easier, faster, and cheaper, better in every way. After 15 years of Jekyll, and spurred by a post on m4, this week I replaced it with a new, custom-built static site generator, dubbed ssg, in “C with templates” C++20. It’s wicked fast, and a complete, cold generation of my blog takes 150ms on my MacBook. That is, it’s done before Ruby would even reach Jekyll’s entry point. entry.title: My Impossible Bucket List
entry.summary:
I wrote this post for a prompt given during our local Indieweb club meeting. See more such posts. My impossible bucket list, things I would want to do/be if the realities of the world and my life did not constrain me. Here it goes: Watch the Sun die. Write a bestseller book about physics. Make them do a good remake of that one anime from the 90s I liked a lot. Finish reading all the books in my to-read list. Get rid of ALL the mosquitoes. Swim across a river. Complete this list. Cycle across a Himalayan pass. Learn how to fly an airplane. Read and understand The Art of Computer Programming. Read a QR code with my eyes. Go back to the house I grew up in. Like C++. Write a journal entry every day. Solve a Millennium Prize Problem. Build a computer from scratch. Get over the Auditory Masking effect. Learn how to make a geographical map from scratch. Take a transcontinental train. Fix my television. Spend a day in the International Space Station. Beat a top player in poker. Watch Daft Punk live. Run an ultra marathon. Get a sleeping score of 100 on my smartwatch. Solve integration problems in my head. Find my first best friend. Learn how to play a Double bass. Drink coffee again. 😔 Become an archaeologist.
